title: Split metering probe for partial-stream handshake and grace credits
creator: Sofia Rivera
description: Run an experiment to evaluate asymmetric per-token metering (separate input vs output rates) combined with a partial-stream handshake that can apply short-session grace credits. Goal is to reduce revenue leakage from tiny streaming sessions and reduce customer complaints about per-stream minimums, while preserving unit economics for high-throughput users.
objective: Determine if split metering plus a 1-2 second partial-stream handshake with a small grace credit reduces short-session churn and improves perceived fairness without materially reducing revenue per active user.
hypothesis: Charging lower or zero ingress (input) rates and applying an output-focused streaming floor with a brief handshake credit will increase conversion for low-duration streaming flows by at least 6% and reduce refund/credit tickets by 30% for customers that use short, interactive streams.
experiment_spec: Cohorts: control (current symmetric IO pricing) vs test (split rates + handshake credit).

Split rates (example): input=$0.0000075/token, output=$0.00011/token for non-streaming; streaming test adds a 10-output-token floor that can be satisfied by a 2-token handshake credit if the session ends within 2s.

Partial-stream handshake: when client opens a streaming session we issue a 2-output-token grace credit; if stream continues beyond 2s and produces more output, normal billing applies and the grace credit is consumed.
Eligibility: new signups and 25% of existing hosted customers who meet usage profile (avg stream <5s historically).
Duration: 6 weeks with interim check at 2 weeks.

Metrics to collect: revenue per active user (RPAU), average tokens billed per session (input/output), short-session conversion rate, tickets/requests for billing disputes, latency and pct of sessions where grace credit applied.
Safety guardrails: automatic rollback if RPAU drops >8% or enterprise churn signal increases above baseline by 1.5x.
acceptance_criteria: Test cohort shows >=6% increase in conversion for short streaming flows without decreasing net RPAU by more than 4% (or a convincing roadmap to recoup via upsells).
Billing correctness: no more than 0.1% of billed sessions have metering inconsistencies in logs during test window.
Support volume: billing dispute tickets related to streaming flow do not increase vs control (ideally drop by >=30%).
Engineering telemetry confirms handshake adds <5ms p50 latency and no impact to overall token throughput on dedicated nodes.
Legal/Finance sign-off on minimum wording and contract language for enterprise customers before wider rollout.
notes: Trade-offs: smaller output floors are friendlier to interactive apps (chatbots, UI assistants) but can be gamed by adversarial clients; handshake reduces gaming surface but requires careful server-side validation.
We are intentionally not changing long-running batch workloads pricing in this experiment; Dedicated customers may opt out via metadata flag.
Design needs microcopy for billing UI showing when a grace credit applied and how floor charging works; PM to draft messaging with Design and Legal.
Eng asks: need a lightweight metering hook to record handshake state and an idempotent billing event so retries don't double-credit.
engineering_notes: ENG sync 2025-02-04: prefer server-side handshake token (opaque id) returned at stream open to track grace credit consumption.
ENG estimate: 5 points for metering + billing pipeline changes, 3 points for telemetry/dashboarding, 2 points for canary rollout plumbing.
Potential refactor: reuse existing prefix/KV caching hooks to avoid adding another state store.
design_feedback: Design 2025-02-06: proposed microcopy for billing modal and API response header that indicates grace credit applied.
Need a small inline explainer in Billing Console: 'Streaming floor and handshake explained' with example math for common session lengths.
legal_finance_notes: Finance 2025-02-10: provided example revenue projections under 3 adoption scenarios (10/30/60% adoption); ROI breakeven at ~27% adoption for the high-sensitivity cohort.
Legal 2025-02-12: requested opt-out clause for enterprise contracts and explicit disclosure in Security Questionnaire answers where billing mechanics affect data egress patterns.
risks: Low-value streams could be abused to run many tiny calls to exploit handshake credit; mitigation: per-tenant rate-limits and anomaly detection.
Accounting complexity for invoices and reconciliation; need Finance to simulate ledger entries for grace credits.
Customer confusion if UI/messaging is incomplete; require quick UX and support playbook.
rollout_plan: Week 0: implement server-side handshake, basic billing changes, and telemetry; internal QA.
Week 1-2: canary with 5% of traffic (non-enterprise) and run smoke checks on revenue and errors.
Week 3-4: expand to 25% cohort, include targeted enterprises that opt in for feedback sessions.
Week 5-6: evaluate metrics and either schedule full rollout, iterate on params, or rollback.
Post-rollout: update billing docs, Pricing FAQ, and enterprise contract templates.
